newsitem.title: UK: Hong Kong stocks edge higher in London trading.
newsitem.headline: Hong Kong stocks edge higher in London trading.

text.p: Hong Kong stocks firmed in London trading on Wednesday, building on the record close in the territory as some investors switch out of other Asian exchanges and into the more liquid Hong Kong market, traders said.
The Hang Seng London Reference Index was up 14.05 points or 0.1 percent at 12,264.62 by 1320 GMT, extending the Hang Seng's earlier 143.81 point, 1.2 percent rise.
HSBC Holdings and Hong Kong Telecom led the advance.
"There seems to have been a reallocation of assets around the region," said a trader at one international brokerage in London.
"People are selling Thailand and the Phillipines and moving into the most liquid market, and the one which is most closely tied to U.S. interest rates, and that is Hong Kong."
But he said there were concerns that the market could find it difficult to build on its recent gains.
"People are getting a bit uncomfortable at the dizzy heights we have reached," the trader said.
